one_month_reasoning: AppLovin's Q3 2026 report is not company-confirmed; third-party calendars put it on Nov 11 (after close), outside the 2026-10-31 window, as is the Nov 16 lead-plaintiff deadline. Inside the window: a possible ruling on AppLovin's TRO application against Unity's Ad Quality SDK (hearing Sep 29-30; a grant would be a small positive for MAX data protection, a denial a small negative and a headline about competition), Meta/Alphabet Q3 prints in late October (ad-demand read-through), the Oct 27-28 FOMC and more sell-side channel-check notes (Edgewater, Wells Fargo pixel data), which have moved the stock 3-5% a day. Unity's own Q3 print is usually early November and probably outside the window. These cut both ways from a 52-week low after a 7-session slide, so I stay neutral: median at spot ($281), lognormal with ~21.5% monthly sigma (75%/3.5), no directional tilt.

fair_value.method: Blend of NTM P/E ($22.2 NTM EPS at Oct-2027 x 15.5 = $344, 45%), EV/NTM EBITDA ($9.1B x 11.5 = $320/sh, 30%) and FCF yield ($21.0 NTM FCF/sh at 6.3% = $333, 25%) = ~$333, ~18% above spot. Single consistent haircut: FY27 revenue/EPS ~3.5% below consensus (Edgewater Q4 gap ~1-2% plus Wells Fargo's later e-commerce ramp), no stacked EBITDA spread haircut.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: FY2027 EPS $19.3 (consensus $20.00 less 3.5%), rolled to NTM at Oct-2027 ~$22.2 (~12% from 3 quarters of ~16% growth plus ~3% buyback accretion) x 15.5x

inputs_detail.value: $20.00 (was $21.16 60 days ago; 19 down / 5 up revisions in 30d)

inputs_detail.derivation: 3.5% haircut, one haircut only: Edgewater's Q4 call (+8-9% q/q, ~$2.25B) is ~1-2% below the ~$2.27-2.28B consensus revenue and its checks call August 'spotty'; Wells Fargo traffic-weighted pixel data pushes the e-commerce ramp to 2027, trimming the 2027 non-gaming contribution by roughly another 2%. Round 1 used 5% while also counting Citi raw merchant counts as an offset; per the supervisor, I drop that offset and the overlap with the EBITDA leg.
$19.3 x 1.16^0.75 (~1.118) for growth decelerating from the 28% FY26->FY27 consensus, x ~1.03 for net share shrink from buybacks ($551M in Q2).

Stock trades ~14x FY27 consensus. 15.5x (from 16x in round 1) gives modest re-rating for ~20% EPS growth and 80%+ EBITDA margins, but the AppLovin-v-Unity Ad Quality suit (Unity calls it a response to 'increased competition and slowing growth') shows competitive pressure escalating, and revisions have not turned. Still far below the 25-30x before the sell-off and above Liftoff's ~7x EV/EBITDA IPO valuation.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: FY2027 EBITDA $8.16B ($10.26B consensus revenue less 3% x 82% margin), rolled to NTM at Oct-2027 ~$9.1B x 11.5x = EV ~$104.9B, less $0.46B net debt, / ~326M shares

inputs_detail.derivation: Same single trim as the EPS leg (Edgewater Q4 gap plus later e-commerce ramp); no extra spread-compression haircut stacked on top, as the supervisor noted round 1 double-counted.
Q3 2026 guide ~83%, Q2 actual 84%; 82% allows for some spread pressure from Unity Vector (guided +19-21% q/q).

Today's EV ~$95B is ~11.2x FY27 consensus EBITDA. 11.5x on NTM is consistent with the 15.5x P/E leg (NTM EPS ~79% of EBITDA per share) with a small discount; Liftoff at ~7x is the floor for a slower, lower-margin peer.
335.3M at Jun 30 2026 less ~9-10M net from buybacks at a ~$2B+/yr pace, net of SBC.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: NTM FCF ~$6.84B (75% of $9.1B EBITDA) / 326M = $21.0/sh at a 6.3% required yield

inputs_detail.derivation: Management expects FCF conversion to normalize to ~75%.
TIKR cites ~6% NTM FCF yield at ~$311; I require slightly more than today's for decelerating growth and rising competition (Unity Vector, the Unity suit).

bear.story: Edgewater is right and more: MAX/Axon share has topped (Sensor Tower already has APP at ~36% of game ad revenue, AdMob 29%), Unity Vector (Q3 Strategic Grow +68-70%) and AdMob compress spreads, the Unity litigation goes badly or signals a data advantage eroding, and e-commerce stays a 'false start' (Wells Fargo) into late 2027. Revenue growth falls to ~15% in 2027, FY27 EPS ~$16, ~11x NTM; class-action headlines persist.

base.story: Q3 in line ($2.06-2.09B), Q4 guide ~+8-10% q/q (near Edgewater/consensus), 2027 revenue +20-24% at ~82% margins; gaming share flat, e-commerce builds slowly through 2027 rather than in 2026. FY27 EPS ~$19.3, multiple ~15x NTM as revision momentum stabilises; buybacks continue.

bull.story: Self-serve Axon and the generative video creative tool gain traction and traffic-weighted e-commerce adoption shows up by mid-2027; the Unity suit protects MAX auction data; growth re-accelerates to 30%, FY27 EPS ~$22, multiple ~20x NTM. Slightly lower than round 1's $520 because Wells Fargo's data pushes the e-commerce payoff late into the horizon.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$185 the stock would trade ~9x FY27 consensus EPS, ~7x EBITDA and a ~10%+ FCF yield with net debt of only ~$0.46B, roughly the multiple of slower, lower-margin Liftoff. A sustained trade there would most likely mean a fundamental break rather than 75%-vol noise: a guide for flat or falling q/q revenue, visible MAX/Axon share loss or a net revenue spread collapse against Unity Vector/AdMob, a loss in the Unity dispute that exposes MAX auction data, a platform (Apple/Google) data-practice action, or a damaging litigation disclosure. Unchanged from round 1; the supervisor's $185 independently agrees.

reasoning: Round 2 changes. The supervisor showed (a) Edgewater's Q4 call is only ~1-2% below consensus revenue, so my 5% EPS cut plus a further 5% EBITDA trim double-counted it; (b) the Citi/Store Leads raw merchant counts I used as an offset are inflated by dormant APAC storefronts: Wells Fargo's traffic-weighted data (which I verified: 85% zero-traffic new sites vs ~30% pre-June, e-commerce 'more like a 2027 story', EW $325 PT) is the better read. I now use one consistent ~3-3.5% trim to FY27 revenue/EPS across all legs and drop the Citi offset. New lane evidence: AppLovin sued Unity (Sep 27-Oct 1) to stop its Ad Quality SDK collecting MAX auction data, with a TRO hearing and a JAMS arbitration; Unity calls it an incumbent's response to 'increased competition and slowing growth'. I read that as confirming that Unity Vector (Q3 Strategic Grow guided +68-70%, Vector >$1B run rate) is a real competitive threat, which justifies trimming the P/E to 15.5x from 16x, though a win would protect MAX's data edge. Sensor Tower still has APP at ~36% of game ad revenue (AdMob 29%) in a game-ad pool growing ~8%, so gaming growth must come from share or pricing. Net: P/E leg $352->$344, EV/EBITDA $309->$320 (double haircut removed, multiple aligned with P/E), FCF $330->$333; blend ~$333, basically unchanged because removing the double count is offset by a lower multiple and the loss of the e-commerce offset. Scenarios 185/325/500 at 30/45/25 (mean ~$327). Ladder: lognormal, median ~$300, sigma 0.57 (below the 75% realized because ~14x EPS, ~6% FCF yield and buybacks give valuation support), with a 3% crash component (median $140) for litigation/fraud-type tails; P(>=281) 0.53. Supervisor facts outside my lane (SEC probe closed, CEO sales under 10b5-1) slightly reduce the governance tail, which is why the crash weight is small. 1-month: no AppLovin earnings in window (est. Nov 11), so neutral around spot at ~21.5% monthly sigma. About 7 follow-up searches/fetches; no option data or priors consulted.
